subject: Implementation blueprint, stability gating & embargo plan
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@beacontrust.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: BeaconTrust Procurement <procurement@beacontrust.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: Implementation approach and canary gating criteria for BeaconTrust rollout

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. As part of our RFP we need a concise implementation blueprint focused on the migration phases, integrations (SAML, KMS, audit logs), and a clear stability gating plan for the canary stage. Key constraints:

- Data residency: production data must remain in us-east-1 for the initial pilot.
- KMS: BeaconTrust requires customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for all persisted artifacts.
- Maintenance windows: limited to weekday 02:00–05:00 ET for production changes.
- Target go-live: phased activation beginning 2027-05-10 with a 2-week canary.

Please include: explicit success/failure gates, observable signal thresholds we can validate, rollback criteria, and a recommended timeline with resource assumptions (hours and roles). Also point us to any pre-flight checks you expect from our side (network, firewall, IAM).

If possible, attach a one-page timeline and a telemetry checklist we can use in our security review. Procurement wants that before they sign off on the SOW.

Appreciate it — Claire

--
Claire Nguyen
Director, Platform Integrations
BeaconTrust
[Attachment requested: one-page timeline, telemetry checklist]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@beacontrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation approach and canary gating criteria for BeaconTrust rollout

Claire —

Thanks for the clarity. Attached is our implementation blueprint (PDF) and a telemetry checklist (Excel) tailored to BeaconTrust constraints. Summary below; full details in attachments.

High-level migration phases (timeline is a recommended minimum):
- Phase 0 (Pre-flight, 2 weeks): network validation, KMS key exchange and IAM mappings, test data seeding in us-east-1 staging.
- Phase 1 (Canary activation, 2 weeks): route 1–5% of production traffic to dedicated canary pool in us-east-1. Daily health review and telemetry sync.
- Phase 2 (Ramp, 1 week): if canary gates pass, expand to 25% then 60% across controlled windows.
- Phase 3 (Cutover & stabilization, 1 week): final traffic reroute and full production monitoring; close-out runbook.

Canary gating & stability measures (pass/fail criteria):
- Error budget: application-level 5xx rate less than 0.1% and increase < 2x baseline.
- Latency: p50/p95 should not degrade more than 20% vs baseline; p99 monitored for spikes.
- Model quality: automated eval on seeded prompt set — no regression > 3% on critical prompts.
- Resource utilization: GPU memory and host CPU within expected envelopes (+/- 10%), no queueing beyond 200ms.
- Security/audit: KMS access logs, vault key usage, and audit events forwarded to BeaconTrust SIEM in near-real time.

Rollback criteria (automatic + manual):
- Automatic: sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes triggers automated traffic diversion to previous model pool.
- Manual: SOC/infra owner may trigger abort on high-severity alerts; documented playbook included.

Observability & telemetry checklist (high level):
- Traces for request lifecycle, token-level latency breakdown, model output confidence scores.
- Daily aggregated dashboards (cost, latency, errors) and a live incident dashboard for the canary.
- Canary telemetry checklist attached as canary-telemetry-checklist.xlsx.

Dependencies and pre-flight items required from BeaconTrust:
- Network: allow outbound to redwood-hosted endpoints in us-east-1; specific IP range and FQDNs in the attached network-topology-diagram.png.
- KMS: provide CMK ARN and IAM role for Redwood to encrypt persisted artifacts; initial test key rotation schedule.
- IAM: OIDC/SAML metadata for SSO and service account bindings for deployment automation.

Staffing assumptions: 40 hours of Redwood integration support during Phases 0–2 (can be increased as part of SOW), with on-call escalation for any overnight canary issues. We can include a 2-week post-go-live hypercare window.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_impl_blueprint_v1.pdf (12 pages)] [Attachment: canary-telemetry-checklist.xlsx] [Attachment: network-topology-diagram.png]

Next steps: If this looks good, we’ll export a one-page timeline for Procurement and prepare an SOW (DocuSign link) that includes optional extra integration hours.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@beacontrust.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: BeaconTrust Procurement <procurement@beacontrust.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:36:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation approach and canary gating criteria for BeaconTrust rollout

Jonas —

Thanks, the attachments look good. Two quick clarifications before Procurement signs the SOW:

1) Canary duration: BeaconTrust security prefers a minimum of 3 weeks for canary observation for infra+security telemetry. Can your gating plan reasonably extend to 3 weeks without impacting the overall go-live date?
2) Maintenance windows: given our 02:00–05:00 ET restriction, can we schedule the heavier cutover steps across two nightly windows to reduce risk?

If the answers are yes, Procurement will move forward with the SOW including requested CMK controls.

Claire
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@beacontrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Implementation approach and canary gating criteria for BeaconTrust rollout

Claire —

Short answers: yes and yes. We updated the one-page timeline to reflect a 3-week canary and split the heavier cutover steps across two nightly maintenance windows inside your 02:00–05:00 ET constraint.

Key changes in the attached one-pager (Drive link below):
- Canary extended to 3 weeks with pre-specified measurement windows at days 3, 7, 14, and 21.
- Cutover split: night 1 — data sync + partial traffic routing (02:00–03:30 ET); night 2 — final traffic shift + validation (03:45–05:00 ET).
- Added an embargo clause: during critical cutover windows we will pause non-essential CI/CD pipelines and block non-admin console sessions to reduce change noise.

We’ll include the extended canary and split-window cadence in the SOW. As a gesture to speed the pilot, Redwood will include 40 hours of complimentary integration engineering time (applies only to Phase 0–2).

Procurement / Legal: we’ve prepared the SOW and DocuSign link (see related_links). Marissa will send the SOW to procurement and coordinate signature and kick-off once we have CMK ARNs and SAML metadata from BeaconTrust.

Marissa / Aditya — please confirm availability for the proposed cutover nights (ET) and that the legal team is copied on the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
[Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-BeaconTrust-Redwood-Impl]
[Attachment: updated_onepager_timeline_v2.pdf]
